Title: Pockets

Title: Tack on Avatar
Content: Objective Temporarily fix a point of a Garment to an Avatar. Location Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Tack Tack on Avatar 3D Toolbar Tack on Avatar Click on a point of a 3D Garment to fix. A point is now being created and a dotted line follows along the mouse cursor, and the selected garment becomes semi-transparent. Click on a point of an Avatar. The selected Garment is now being opaque once again. Same tack is now being created in the corresponding 2D Pattern. Activate Simulate. The Garment is now being simulated while the two points are being fixed to the Avatar.

Title: Change Pose by OBJ Morphing
Content: Objective Vertex Morphing has a merit of maintaining avatar's final form without any distortion. However on the other hand, garments may fall off during the morphing process, especially when there is a large difference between the first and the last pose as the pose changes by the minimum distances between points in the avatar rather than the units of avatar joints. Therefore if a big difference between the poses, it is recommended to create an OBJ file for interim pose and morph stage-by-stage. If it is inconvenience, change pose by another method, Change Pose by Using Collada. Operation After dressing an avatar in CLO, at least two files are required to change poses such as T-pose avatar and another avatar in desired pose. Export both of the files in OBJ format. To find export method in details, check 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export for the reference. Click File Import OBJ and select the T-pose OBJ file of the previously exported avatar. Click OK on the option dialogue to load the avatar. Put the garments on top of the loaded avatar. Click File Import OBJ Load as Morph Target the previously saved avatar with another pose. Set the 'Morphing Frame Count' in the option dialogue, then click OK. The Simulation button automatically activates and the avatar pose slowly changes according to the set frame count. The garment also starts simulating in accordance with the change. Adjust garments if necessary, after the final pose simulation.

Title: HASP Error Message
Content: Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) Cause of Error The Server and Client PCs are unable to communicate with each other. Solution 1. Type 'services.msc' in the Run window. 2. In the Service window that follows, check whether or not the status of the Sentinel LDK License Manager is Running. If the status is not Running, right-click and select Start. If the status is Started, right-click and select Restart. Reboot. 3. If this does not solve the problem, check both versions of the Server and Client PCs HASP Drivers. Make sure both versions are the same. You are able to check the version under Diagnostics. 4. If this does not work, ask your Network Administrator to confirm the Port communication status between the Server and Client. Check whether the 1947 Port is being used by another program. Feature not found (H0031) Cause of Error Despite the dongle key has been recognized, the Feature ID of the program and the Feature ID of the dongle key are different. (This occurs when the wrong version of Marvelous Deisnger is installed - i.e. installed the Stand-Alone version for a Network dongle key, and vice versa) Solution Make sure the correct version of Marvelous Designer is installed. ex&gt Purchased the Network version, but used the Stand-Alone version's installer. -&gt Re-install Marvelous Designer using the Network version's installer. Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) Cause of Error When the HASP Key is not plugged into the PC. Network Version only: the Client PC does not recognize the Server PC that the dongle key is connected to. When the HASP Key is recognized, but the Sentinel License Manager service fails to start properly. Solution Make sure the HASP is connected to the PC. Check the red light of the HASP Key. It should light up when plugged in to the PC. Check whether or not the HASP Key shows up in the ACC page (refer to the image below) If the red light or the ACC page does not look equal to the image above, refer to the following manual, reinstall the Sentinel HASP Driver. HASP Driver Installation Too many concurrent users (H0038) Cause of Error When the number of users connected to the program exceeds the maximum allowed number of users. ex&gt If the maximum number of users (the number of purchased licenses) is 2, and 3 users try to log-in, the last person to attempt a connection will receive an error message. Solution Check the number of current users via the link below. Connect when one of the current users exit the program. ACC Page Click Sentinel Keys, on the left. When the Key shows up as the image above, click Sessions, on the right. The following page should display the current user(s). Connect when one of the current users exits the program. If any unauthorized user is connected, click the Disconnect button on the right to log the person out of the program. Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) Cause of Error The HASP Driver has not been properly installed on the PC, or the Driver is damaged. To confirm whether it is properly installed, enter http://localhost:1947 or http://127.0.0.1:1947 into your web browser, or click on the following link ( ACC Page ). If the following page does not look equal to the image below, there is a problem with the Sentinel HASP Driver. Solution Refer to the following manual and reinstall the HASP Driver. HASP Driver Installation

Title: Offset Pattern Outline
Content: Objective Extend or retract (ver MD10) the Pattern outline while maintaining its original shape. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu Offset Pattern Outline Operation With the Transform Pattern tool or the Edit Pattern tool, select the entire or partial Pattern outline. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu Offset Pattern Outline The Offset Pattern Outline Window appears. Adjust following options as needed. Option Description Direction Extend Extend Pattern Outlines. Retract Retract Pattern Outlines. (ver MD10) Note: Only Distance can be modified when Retract is selected. Distance Set how much in distance the Pattern outline is extended. Number of Offsets Set the number of offsets to be created. Total Distance Total Distance = Distance x Number of Offsets Create Internal Line Create Internal Lines at where the original Pattern outlines existed. Side Segment Type Perpendicular Extends the Pattern outline perpendicular to the selected Pattern outline. Extend Side Segments Extends the Pattern outline while matching the angles of the segments on either side. Mirror Extends the Pattern outline based on the corner angle created with the selected Pattern outline and its adjacent one. Default Corner Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern. Right Angled Corner Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or Pattern and converting corners to right angles. Unfilled Corner Extends the Pattern outline all around the selected segment or pattern, except for corners. Click OK. The Pattern outlines are offset according to the settings. Curve points are optimized automatically. (ver MD10)

Title: M:N Segment Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Easily sew multiple segments (M) to multiple segments (N) at once and edit them as a group. When the total length of multiple segments corresponding to M is different from the total length of multiple segments corresponding to N, N segments are divided in proportion to M segments. Location Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing Note: Hold down the Segment Sewing tool for a while to access the M:N Segment Sewing tool. Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing M:N Segment Sewing 2D Toolbar M:N Segment Sewing Click on the segments belong to M segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete M sewing lines. M sewing lines are highlighted in neon color. As checking the Directional Notches, establish Sewing Lines on N segments. Then, hit the Enter key on the keyboard to complete. The Sewing Lines no longer appear in neon color. Note: While establishing M:N sewing lines, hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the last action or hit the Esc key on the keyboard to cancel all actions. When you click on an inappropriate segment while sewing, the segment appears in red and you cannot establish Sewing Line on the selected segment. The length difference of the first and the second half of seams appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. When the difference is greater than 1 inch, it appears in red to alert the user.

Title: Edit Graphic Size (Property Editor)
Content: Objective Use the Property Editor to resize graphics. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Texture (2D) / Transform Graphic 2D Toolbar Edit Texture (2D) /Transform Graphic Operation Follow the indicated guideline in Location Select the graphic to be edited. The selected graphic's properties appear in the Property Editor. Find the Graphic Transformation category. Properties Description Information Name/Item No. Enter a name or an item number of the graphic. Classification Assign the graphic type among Embroidery, Logo, Print, Wash (Jeanologia). Material Configure the graphic's material, texture, color, and transparency. Graphic Configuration Face Place the graphic on the front, back, or both sides. Over Seamline (ver MD10) Place the graphic on the seam of patterns. Note: - Graphic does not appear when the difference of the seam is over the allowable extent. - Graphic may not be matching when it is placed over the curves. It this case, deactivate this option and adjust the graphic manually. Tile Tile the graphic along the X or Y axis of a Pattern while maintaining its original size. Note: The same option is available in the right-click pop-up menu. Graphic Transformation Adjust the rotation angle, width, height, and Z-Offset(ver MD10) of the graphic.

Title: Initial setup/options when first-launching the software
Content: Objective Version -Enterprise Network (Online Authentication) -Academic Perpetual (Online Authentication) Operation Double-click on the icon on the Desktop to launch the program. The login pop-up window appears as below. Enter ID and password. Adjust the options as needed and select Log In. Left click on the drop-down arrow to access further options. Save ID Save the entered ID in the registry. Save PW Save the entered password in the registry. If using 'Firewall', Please check this option in the login window Login through the client server. Use Proxy Server (This option not available from MD11 on) When user uses the proxy server, the proxy server information is needed to be properly certified. To use the proxy server, toggle on the check box and enter corresponding proxy information. Note: To use proxy server, please toggle on Use Proxy Server and enter proxy information. Adjust below options as needed. Units Set default unit. Language Set default language View Control Choose View Control presets optimized for respective mouse and program type. To adjust the setting individually, navigate to Settings User Settings View Control. Graphic Options Antialiasing Adjust the setting to smooth out the outline of the object. As the value increases, smoother the outline is and slower the rendering speed is. Show Shadow Show or hide shadow in the 3D Window. Use VBOs Set VBOs usage to improve the rendering speed. Use Normal Maps Use or unuse Normal Maps which express seamlines and textures more realistically. Select OK to run the program.

Title: Deactivate/Activate Avatar
Content: Objective Deactivate or activate avatars as needed. When it is deactivated, the garments do not recognize while simulation (ver2.3.0). Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up menu (Right-click on Avatar) Deactivate/Activate Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up menu (Right-click on Avatar) Deactivate/Activate Avatar Avatar is now being deactivated/activated.

Title: FILE: Export Joint Keyframe Animation with FBX
Content: Objective Allows users to export both the garment and avatar together, without losing joint animation. The joint animation is currently exported with keys at every frame for the duration of the motion. Location File Export FBX Option Joint Animation Operation Import an FBX containing a rigged character with joint animation as an Avatar, with the box next to 'Joint Animation' checked (found under the "Object" section). Create a garment for the character, or add a garment option from the Library, at a desired pose from the Avatar's animation. Simulate in the 3D Window to drape the garment onto the Avatar. Once complete, navigate to the File menu location, select 'Export', then select 'FBX'. Choose 'Export All' in the Export FBX pop-up window. Click on 'OK'. Open the resulting FBX file in another 3D software package. Observe that the Avatar's joint animation has been exported (keyed at every frame).

Title: Are the Adobe Illustrator curves able to be imported and edited in Marvelous Designer?
Content: No, they are not. The curves from Adobe Illustrator cannot be imported into Marvelous Designer.

Title: Mirror Paste Button
Content: Objective Copy and mirror paste buttons (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click on the copied button then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click on a desired location to paste the buttons. Note: Before pasting buttons in place, right-click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttons can be manually input for multiple copy and paste. When buttons are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.

Title: Show/Hide Bond/Skive
Content: Objective Show or hide bonded or skived area in the 3D window (ver2.3.0). Location 3D Trims Display Icon Show Bond/Skive Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Trims Display Icon Show Bond/Skive The selected area's bond/skive in the 3D window is now being shown or hidden.

Title: Add Point or Curve Point to Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Use the right-click pop-up menu to add a point or curve point to modify Lines (Avatar). Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) When the Avatar is draped in a Garment, the Garment becomes translucent. Right click on the Line (Avatar) where a point or curve point should be added. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Choose Add Point or Add Curve Point as needed. Add Point: a segment point is added to the selected line. Add Curve Point: a curve point is added to the selected line. Select and move the added point or curve point by using the Edit Line (Avatar) tool to edit Line (Avatar).

Title: Create Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Draw lines on an Avatar and extract Patterns. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Line (Avatar) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Line (Avatar) If there is a Garment on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Hover the mouse over the Avatar. A black dot follows the mouse. Click on the desired position on the Avatar to create lines or shapes. The lines or shapes appear on the Avatar in black. Click on the start point to complete drawing the line. The lines or shapes are created on the Avatar. Note: To create a curve point while drawing lines on the Avatar, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard and click on the Avatar. Hit the Delete key on the keyboard to cancel the latest action or hit the Esc key or Ctrl+Z to cancel all actions. All lines and shapes drawn on the Avatar are saved when you save the file in Project, Garment, or Avatar file format.

Title: Edit Line (Avatar)
Content: Objective Edit lines created on an Avatar. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) Operation Select/Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Click on the line or the shape to be selected. The line or the shape is selected and highlighted in yellow. While the line of the shape is selected, click and drag to move the selected item to the desired position. Delete Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Edit Line (Avatar) 3D Toolbar Edit Line (Avatar) If a Garment is on the Avatar, the Garment appears translucent. Select the line or the shape to be deleted. Right click on the selected item and select Delete or hit the Delete key on the keyboard. The selected line or shape is deleted. Note: To select multiple lines or shapes, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard, then click on additional lines or shapes. To select all lines and shapes on the Avatar, hit the Ctrl+A on the keyboard. After the lines and shapes are drawn on the Avatar, if you delete the Avatar, all previously created lines, and shapes are also deleted.

Title: Lock Remesh Patterns
Content: Objective Lock patterns from selection based on whether or not they are dynamic Marvelous Designer patterns with adjustable particle distance and curve points, or remeshed patterns created with the Topology Tools &amp Remesh All. Location 2D Pattern Window Lock Pattern Drop-down Menu Lock All Remesh Patterns Operation Load a garment. Create topology with the 'Create Topology' Tool in the 2D Pattern Window. When complete, with blue retopology still visible, Right Mouse Button Click in the 2D Pattern Window then select 'Remesh All (duplicate)'. Retopology meshes are placed directly on top of the original patterns. Click on 'Lock All Remesh Patterns' in the Lock Pattern drop-down menu within the 2D Window to lock all remeshed patterns from selection. Click and move original patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool. Click on 'Unlock All Remesh Patterns' to release the selection mask. Click on 'Lock All Pattern Outlines' and 'Lock All Internal Lines' to lock original patterns from selection. Click and move remeshed patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool.

Title: Seamline Topstitch (ver MD10)
Content: Objective Create a Seamline Topstitch. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Seamline Topstitch 2D Toolbar Seamline Topstitch Operation Follow the indicated guideline above. All sewing lines on the Pattern are displayed. Click on a point where a Topstitch begins. Move mouse to the direction where the Topstitch is going to be created. Click on another point where the Topstitch ends. The Topstitch is now being created with being highlighted. Note: Click and drag in the 2D window to encompass all segments where Topstitches to be applied. Topstitches appear on all selected segments. Use lasso selection to select Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Topstitches should be created on. OBJ Topstitches temporarily disappear when the Simulation is activated, but they appear again when the Simulation is deactivated. Right click when creating the Topstitch to enter specific length.

Title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Rendering Thickness
Content: Objective Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as the default value, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. Note: To see the rendering thickness, the 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on Thick Textured Surface. Location Fabric Unit Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Operation Fabric Unit Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Fabric Fabric Item Property Editor Thickness Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied. Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0) Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Rendering Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Shortcut keys, menus, graphic options, view controls, default files, font settings and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. Title: Complete Nonlinear Simulation
Content: Objective This function allows more accurate Simulation on fabric stretch (ver3.0.0). It is especially effective for longer Garments. Note: This is available from ver3.0.0 onward. Location 3D Garment Window Right-click Pop-up Menu Simulation Properties Property Editor Nonlinear Simulation Operation Follow the indicated guideline below and check the Nonlinear Simulation On: 3D Garment Window Simulation Property Editor Preset Complete (Nonlinear) Fabric strength and elongation are now being simulated more accurately.

Title: Where can Marvelous Designer be useful?
Content: Marvelous Designer has a variety of applications in the world of 3D clothing design. It is most useful in situations where garment detail and quality are paramount. The more complex the design, the more time you can save using Marvelous Designer. Since MD provides several import/export options, users can work with Marvelous Designer with various 3D software programs. Please refer to compatible file formats. Link

Title: CREATE CUSTOM BUTTON TEXTURE: Create Button Texture
Content: Objective Create and apply custom textures to buttons in CLO in order to express various button styles. Note: Adobe Photoshop is needed to create custom button texture. Operation Download custom button texture templates (.psd) provided in the Library window: Note: Choose your desired button design and download respective custom button texture file as needed. Open downloaded .psd file in Adobe Photoshop. The template is divided into three parts each representing front, back, and thread of the button. Open a texture image to be embedded to the template. The texture will open in a new tab in Adobe Photoshop. Follow the path: Main Menu Edit Define Pattern The selected texture will be added as a pattern in Adobe Photoshop. In the Layer Window, select the desired layer to be painted with the defined pattern. The Layer Window is located along the right side of the Adobe Photoshop Window. While the desired layer is selected, left click on the Paint tool and select the defined pattern The selected layer will be painted with the chosen pattern. Hide UV and Test layers, then save the image. Note: Saving the image in .jpeg format is recommended.

Title: Merge Symmetric Patterns
Content: Objective Merge symmetric Patterns into a single Pattern. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) Merge Operation Navigate to 2D toolbar and select Edit Pattern tool. Right click on the Pattern outline of either symmetric Pattern and follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern Outline) Merge The symmetric Patterns are merged into a single Pattern as their Linked Editing function is removed. Note: When there is any point on the selected segment to merge Patterns, the Patterns cannot be merged.

Title: MODULAR MODE: Module Structure
Content: Module is a system that allows you to adjust the designs easily and combine them part by part. Please see the terminology for the Module below in order to have a better understanding in the Modular Mode. A: Module Structure: A state when a Block Box that consists of a Garment is sewn to another. When sewing a Block Box that is in this Block Structure to a Pattern, it automatically creates Sewing Lines in between the Patterns as it is already interlocked. B: Pattern: Patterns to be included in a Block that will be adjusted partially. Patterns in the Modular Mode can be modified and sewn the same as the Simulation Mode. C: Block Box: A frame that consists of a Module Structure. D: Block: A state when Patterns are sewn to Block Boxes. Blocks that have the same Block Boxes can be replaced with each other.

Title: 3D Snapshot
Content: Objective Save 3D window snapshots from one angle in image file format. Location Main Menu File Snapshot 3D Window (F10) Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Snapshot 3D Window (F10) Save File pop-up window appears. 2. Enter desired file name and location, then click Save. Snapshot window appears. 3. Set details as needed: Single View Image Size Preset Customize or select from provided preset options. Orientation Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. Width Set the width of the image. Height Set the height of the image. Unit Sets the unit of measurement for the image. Resolution Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. Option Transparent Background Save the image with transparent background. Save HTML File A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. (ver MD10) Reset Resets the options back to the program default settings. Note: Garment Measurements can now be captured in 3D snapshots (ver4.1.0). In order to include Garment Measurements, toggle on the Show Garment Measurements icon in the 3D window.
